title: Grateful Dead Live at Woodstock Music  on 1969-08-16
lineage: Panasonic SV-3700 > Cardas cable S/PDIF > Edirol UA-5 > analog out > Korg MR-1 DFF @ [1bit/2.8 mhz] Rate Conversion: AudioGate to [24bit/96 khz] Mastering: In WaveLab with L3 Waves Multimaximizer Rate Conversion with r8brain to [16bit/44.1 khz] > TLH > Flac

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of Woodstock's infamous show, highlighted by a monster 45‑minute Lovelight despite an uneven overall performance.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as a remarkable upgrade – crystal‑clear soundboard audio that makes even the chaotic Woodstock environment listenable. Musically the set is notorious for its early missteps (a two‑minute St Stephen, a limp Mama Tried and a Dark Star that never really launches), but Pigpen’s 45‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight and Jerry’s soaring guitar leads turn it into a memorable slice of history.

ai_rating.rationale: Multiple reviewers give the recording top marks for sound quality (5‑star praise) while opinions on the performance range from “worst ever” to enthusiastic love of Lovelight; the strong technical score and standout moments outweigh the overall uneven show.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with a notable upgrade over previous releases; no major drop‑outs reported, captures long Lovelight and occasional crowd ambience cleanly.

standout_songs: Mama Tried (noted as good by a reviewer)
poor_songs: Dark Star (fails to launch according to one review)
Mama Tried (described as limp by another reviewer)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Chaotic early set with a very short St Stephen, a long break, radio‑crosstalk and a sprawling Lovelight that dominates the second half; transitions feel uneven but the epic Lovelight provides a unifying climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his guitar work – “every note” and “stinging leads” were highlighted as highlights of the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for bizarre radio transmissions from his bass amp during Lovelight, adding a quirky moment to the performance.
band_member_comments.Keys: The Hammond organ is described as “swirly psychedelic” and beautiful, especially on Dark Star.
